text: The moon shone soft upon the quiet shore.
Sunny walked where gentle waves rolled in.
Along the sand, a tiny waddling shape
came home from fishing in the silver sea.
A little penguin, blue and white and small,
with flippers soft and feet that padded slow.
It shook the water gently from its coat
and waddled up the beach toward its burrow.
“Hello,” said Sunny. “Have you been for a swim?”
“All day,” it said. “And now it's time for bed.”
It waddled slowly up the moonlit sand,
leaving tiny footprints in a row.
“My burrow's warm and cosy in the dune,”
the little penguin said with sleepy eyes.
They watched the waves roll softly on the shore,
the moon a silver path across the sea.
The little penguin gave a gentle yawn
and tucked its flippers close against its side.
It settled in its burrow, snug and deep,
safe among the grasses on the dune.
Sunny found a hollow in the sand,
warm and soft beneath the tufts of grass.
The waves sang low their whispering lullaby.
Everything was gentle, calm, and safe.
Her eyes grew heavy as the tide came in.
One slow blink… then another… then no more.
And Sunny slept beside the sleeping penguin,
rocked by dreams as soft as rolling waves.
Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, little penguin.
Goodnight, sleepy sea. Goodnight, little one.
